prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat electronic bands at a magic twist angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, which opened the field of moire quantum materials

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B046 alone with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer. Having read all eight round-1 statements and the chair's summary, I find that the scientific case has not weakened and the disputes are mainly about weighting, as the chair says. The achievement is a prediction (flat bands at a magic angle, 2011) followed by an experimental discovery (correlated insulating and superconducting states, 2018) that created a gate-tunable platform for correlated and topological physics. It was then reproduced and extended by independent groups in several moire systems. Prediction, discovery and consequence are all documented, and the three credited names map onto the decisive theory and the decisive experiment. The chair's summary shows that B046 and B041 are each other's nearest rivals and not opposed camps, so my choice rests on what kind of achievement each is. B046 exposed new physics in a new class of materials, whereas B041 improves, by a large and impressive factor, the measurement of a quantity that earlier prizes had already opened up. I would ask that the citation say the experimental discovery was made by the Jarillo-Herrero group, so that it does not read as the work of one person.
statement.case_against: The most serious objection is maturity. Eight years after the experiment, the pairing mechanism is open, twist-angle disorder still limits reproducibility in some respects, and the credit omits Yuan Cao as first author and the parallel groups of Dean, Yacoby, Young and Fatemi, as well as earlier twisted-bilayer theory by Santos and Peres. Within the three-name limit these omissions cannot be repaired by choice of names, only softened by wording in the citation. B041 has the cleaner two-name attribution and a longer track record, and B001 has three decades of confirmation, so a colleague who weights maturity and tidy credit above scope has a principled reason to rank B046 lower. I do not think that reason is wrong in kind, only that I weight it less than the opening of a new field.

responses.point: Lindroth argues that B041 is mature, well attributed and distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, because the physics lies in atomic-structure control (magic wavelength, blackbody, hyperfine and collisional shifts) behind the 1e-18 accuracy budget. She also says it should be cited as the neutral-atom lattice scheme and not as clocks in general.
responses.response: That is the best statement of the B041 case and I accept most of it. The magic-wavelength idea is original, the systematic-shift control is real physics, and the attribution to two names is cleaner than anything in my own configuration. I also accept that the 2005 prize supplies the optical counting and that the lattice scheme is a separate step. Where we still differ is on what the step is. The accuracy budget establishes how well we can know a transition frequency, whereas B046 revealed a set of phases of matter that were not expected in a carbon system and that now serve as a platform for several new problems. I weight discovery of new phenomena above a further order of magnitude in measurement, which is why B041 is my first alternative and not my choice. On her point about redefinition of the second, I consider it a reason for B041 to be recognised later at no cost to its merits, not a reason to hold B046 back.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair and a B041 supporter, says B041 is in part a refinement of the already recognised 2005 and 2012 lines, that its payoff (the redefinition of the second) has not yet happened, and that B046 maturity concerns (pairing, uncredited first authors) could be small enough for its wider support to prevail.
responses.response: I appreciate that Pearce states the overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes as the strongest objection to his own preferred ballot, and I agree with it more than he does. I would answer his last uncertainty directly: the maturity problems of B046 are real but they concern interpretation and completeness of credit, not whether the phenomenon exists. Correlated insulators and superconductivity at the magic angle have been reproduced by independent groups and extended to other moire platforms, so the discovery is not in doubt. I also agree with him that broad opening support is not an argument in itself. For that reason I would not claim a mandate from five top-three placements; I rest on the structure of the achievement. I would also ask the committee to note that his citation emphasis on accuracy and stability, versus Kroll's and Lindroth's emphasis on invention, shows that B041 supporters have not yet fixed what the recognised step is, and that is a less secure position for a final citation.

responses.point: Olsson places B032 (topological insulators) first and B046 as her strongest rival. She worries that the microscopic origin of the superconductivity is unsettled, that sample variability is real, and that the omitted experimentalists cannot be repaired within three names. She also wonders whether B032 beats B046 on maturity once the Mele and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang credit issue is considered.
responses.response: I agree with her on the cautious wording of the citation, and I have kept my own citation to correlated insulating and superconducting states and made no claim about the mechanism. I would go further: the committee should cite only what independent laboratories have reproduced. On B032 I see real maturity and a rich experimental record, but her own uncertainty about Mele and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang is, to my mind, a larger attribution problem than the one in B046. Four names in the credited set also exceed what a three-person configuration can hold without dropping someone whose contribution is decisive. For that reason I keep B032 out of my alternatives this round, although my first-principles view of topological band structure makes me regard it as a serious candidate for a later year.

responses.point: Mehlig keeps B001 (dynamical mean-field theory) as his sole configuration, defending its conceptual originality and over thirty years of confirmation, while acknowledging that it lacks experimental drama and that Metzner is omitted from the credited trio.
responses.response: I agree that B001 has the strongest maturity case on the shortlist, and I have kept it as an alternative for that reason. I also agree that a theory-led achievement is not disqualified for lacking experimental drama. My difficulty is that the attribution gap he names is, if anything, larger than he allows: Metzner and, on my recollection, Muller-Hartmann are both outside the trio, and I cannot verify priority details from the supplied record. A three-name limit forces a choice that I could not defend as fully as I can the B046 trio. I also note that DMFT is a method whose value is its reach across materials, and I am close to that community through my own work, which is a further reason for me to leave the lead on this ballot to colleagues. If the committee finds B046 premature, B001 would be my fallback, with the Metzner question resolved explicitly before any vote.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will regard eight years since the 2018 experiment as sufficient when the pairing mechanism is open; this is the main point on which my judgement and that of colleagues who prefer B041 or B001 genuinely differ.
Whether three names, with a citation referring to the Jarillo-Herrero group, represent the experimental side fairly without Yuan Cao and the parallel groups.
How much a possible future redefinition of the second should count for B041, and whether my view of its novelty of principle is fair to the atomic-physics colleagues.

My recollection of the priority details for DMFT (Metzner, Muller-Hartmann) and for earlier twisted-bilayer theory (Santos and Peres) comes from memory and cannot be checked against the supplied material.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B046 or B041. For B001, my own work uses electronic-structure methods including density functional theory and dynamical mean-field theory, so I am professionally close to that community, although my profile documents no personal or institutional tie to Georges, Vollhardt or Kotliar. I would flag that closeness and consider stepping back if the committee turns to B001.
